brief.headline: Push for ₹28,644 annual savings by matching the ₹1.87/NOS price we already pay Suraj Blow Plast for the same PET bottle.

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹1.87/NOS we pay Suraj Blow Plast for the PET BOT AMBER 100ML bottle.
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹2.18/NOS — 16.6% more than the ₹1.87/NOS we already pay Suraj Blow Plast for the identical item. No reason to pay more for the same bottle.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from 30 days after receipt to paying within 15 days, in exchange for a 5% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹46,539 of our cash, but we get back roughly 5% (their borrowing rate is 10.27%, so 15 days early is worth about half that annualized) — ask for a 5% cut to make it worthwhile for us.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is healthy — [ICRA] A / Stable rating, they keep ₹3.80 of every ₹100 they sell, and they have ₹35.20 Cr free cash last year. But their cash is stuck for 79 days (they collect from customers in 67 days, pay suppliers in only 17 days), so cash is tighter than similar firms (79 days vs peer 79 days — tied). The catch: we're tiny to them — ₹11.32 L is just 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue. On our own we have almost no pull, but they do have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays on record, so they may want to keep every customer happy. Play the long game: commit more volume or a longer contract, and line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a credible second source to show you're serious about switching if the price doesn't move.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹2.18/NOS for the PET bottle; we pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the same item — a 16.6% gap.
Closing that gap saves us ₹28,644 a year.
They borrow money at about 10.27%, so paying them 15 days early is worth roughly 5% annualized to them.
We're 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — tiny on our own.
They have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays on their record.
evidence.figure: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

evidence.point: Market reference: 28 mm PP caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — shows packaging has room to flex on price.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate already vetted for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma; strong and profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): PET resin manufacturer in East India — could supply preforms or bottles direct; medium confidence.

risks: We're only 0.02% of their business — they may not care enough to move on price unless we bundle more SKUs or commit longer term.
They're in the grey zone on the distress measure (Altman Z 2.77) and have GST/EPF delays — push too hard and a fragile supplier could stumble; balance the price ask with supply security.
We have no SKU-level volume data in hand — if the ₹28,644 saving is spread over tiny orders, the admin cost of switching may eat the gain; confirm order size before you commit to a new source.
Alternates like Manjushree and Mold-Tek are much bigger — they may have higher minimums or longer lead times than TPAC; qualify terms before using them as leverage.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to grow with you, but right now we're paying you ₹2.18 for a bottle we buy elsewhere at ₹1.87 — let's find a way to close that gap and talk about a longer commitment.
